current_generic_selection_loss.caption: Generic-to-Native selection on 203 verified paired cuts in 21 model/device groups; 0 groups have fewer than two cuts. No quality filter. Hollow markers denote one candidate, which provides no ranking test. Every nonempty group has equal weight. Original Native FPS and historical Native quality retain their separate observed contracts.

marker_policy.one_candidate: hollow backend marker; no ranking test

fastest_deployment_tradeoff.caption: Throughput and energy of each model's fastest split relative to its globally fastest Full. Both axes use the same exact Full configuration. Right of one is faster and below one uses less energy per image. These throughput-selected points are not the full Pareto front or an energy-minimum selection. Quality eligibility does not establish equal accuracy or identical runtime costs. Text positions alone are displaced for readability; there are no inferred confidence intervals.

fastest_split_baseline_comparison.caption: The same selected fastest split with two Full references. A connection changes only the denominator, not the split or its speed. Global Full means the fastest actual Full configuration across hosts; same-host Full means the fastest Full on the split's physical host. Labels round factors to two decimals; plot data retain unrounded values and exact UIDs. The paper profile applies the numerical 5% CPU-relative quality rule. Its winners match the broad current view for this generation.

quality_generic_selection_loss.caption: Generic-to-Native selection on 186 verified paired cuts in 21 model/device groups; 0 groups have fewer than two cuts. Both Native historical numerical quality and current bound Generic quality pass. Hollow markers denote one candidate, which provides no ranking test. Every nonempty group has equal weight. Original Native FPS and historical Native quality retain their separate observed contracts.

marker_policy.one_candidate: hollow backend marker; no ranking test

resnet_h8_energy_current.caption: ResNet-50/H8: current throughput and calibrated system energy for all Native splits and both Full alternatives. The annotated cuts are selected independently by maximum FPS and minimum energy. FPS is the stored performance-cohort median; energy is mean per-repeat E/N in mJ/image. Performance and energy come from separate runs of the same configuration; energy-window rates are not substituted.

selector_loss_heatmap.caption: Historical graph-score comparison: Native throughput loss for six selectors in fixed model/setup groups. Every column uses the same historical Native reference measurements within a row. Parentheses give candidate counts; column headers count exact/tie-aware winner agreements. The stored hardware-fit profile is the H10 profile on every setup. The historical reported YOLOv7 Native overlay and archived Generic records remain separate from current A4 deployments. No current quality filter is applied to this historical cohort.
